Breaking: Ancient DNA may survive extreme heat far longer than scientists thought — South African cave discovery raises big questions 🔬🧬

Key points
- A recent find in a South African cave suggests ancient DNA can persist under hot conditions much longer than previously assumed.
- If confirmed, this would change baseline expectations for where and when we might recover human or environmental DNA.
- Implications for field sampling strategy, lab protocols, and how we interpret “DNA survival limits.”

Why it matters
- Rethinks thermal limits for preserved genetic material.
- Could expand viable recovery windows at warmer sites.
- Puts pressure on contamination controls and reference datasets.

Bottom line
This isn’t just a technical tweak — it challenges assumptions about how long DNA can last in heat, potentially opening new chapters in paleogenetics and archaeology.
